title: Payment Integrity Information Act of 2019
official_summary:
Payment Integrity Information Act of 2019

This bill reorganizes and revises several existing improper payments statutes, which establish requirements for federal agencies to cut down on improper payments made by the federal government.

The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) may establish one or more pilot programs to test potential accountability mechanisms for compliance with requirements regarding improper payments and the elimination of improper payments.

The bill requires the OMB to update its plan for improving the death data maintained by the Social Security Administration and improving federal agency use of death data.

The bill establishes an interagency working group on payment integrity.

summary.headline: Congress reorganized federal rules on improper government payments and added pilot programs, death-data updates, and a payment integrity working group.
summary.what_it_does: This law combines and rewrites several older statutes that require federal agencies to reduce improper payments, meaning money paid out by mistake or in the wrong amount. It lets the Office of Management and Budget set up one or more pilot programs to test ways to hold agencies accountable for meeting those requirements. It also requires OMB to update its plan for improving death records kept by the Social Security Administration and for how federal agencies use that death data. Finally, it creates an interagency working group focused on payment integrity.

who_it_affects.how: They must follow the reorganized improper payment requirements and may take part in pilot programs testing accountability methods.
Agencies are directed to use better death records to help prevent payments from going out to people who have died.

who_it_affects.group: Families of deceased people receiving federal payments
who_it_affects.how: Improved death-data sharing may affect how quickly federal payments are stopped after a person dies.
